reference_drawer.title: 📖 Formula & Theorem Guide
reference_drawer.description: Key theorems and algebraic rules for Proof of Irrationality in CBSE Class 10.

items.rule: If prime p divides a², then p divides a (where a is a positive integer).
Two integers a and b are coprime if their greatest common divisor is 1: gcd(a, b) = 1.
Sum, difference, product, and quotient of rational numbers are always rational.
items.formula: r_1, r_2 \in \mathbb{Q} \implies r_1 \pm r_2 \in \mathbb{Q}, \; r_1 r_2 \in \mathbb{Q}, \; \frac{r_1}{r_2} \in \mathbb{Q} \; (r_2 \neq 0)

concepts.title: 1. What is an Irrational Number?
concepts.subtitle: Definition & Proof by Contradiction
concepts.summary: A real number that cannot be written in the form a/b where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0 is irrational.

points.text: Proof Method: We use Proof by Contradiction: assume rational, deduce that gcd(a, b) ≥ p, contradicting coprimality.

concepts.trap: Never forget to state that a and b are COPRIME integers with gcd(a, b) = 1.

concepts.title: 2. Theorem 1.2: Prime Divisibility
concepts.subtitle: If p | a² then p | a
concepts.summary: Let p be a prime number. If p divides a², then p divides a, where a is a positive integer.

points.text: Key Theorem: If 2 divides a², then 2 divides a (so a = 2c).
Crucial Role: Connects squaring equation a² = pb² back to linear factor divisibility.

concepts.formula: p \text{ is prime}, \; p \mid a^2 \implies p \mid a
concepts.trap: This theorem ONLY holds true when p is a PRIME number.

concepts.title: 3. Linear Surd Combinations (a ± b√c)
concepts.subtitle: Rational Closure Property
concepts.summary: Sum, difference, product, and quotient of rational numbers are always rational.

points.text: Rearrangement: Transpose constants to isolate radical √c = (a - kb)/(mb).
Contradiction: RHS is purely rational while LHS is known to be irrational.

concepts.trap: Do not square both sides for linear forms like 3 + 2√5 when √5 is already given as irrational.

concepts.title: 4. Sum of Two Radicals (√a + √b)
concepts.subtitle: Double Radical Isolation Strategy
concepts.summary: Set equal to rational x, transpose one radical, square both sides, and isolate the remaining radical.

points.text: Step 2: Square: b = x² - 2x√a + a, then isolate √a = (x² + a - b)/(2x).

concepts.trap: Always transpose one surd before squaring to avoid cross-products of two surds.
